title: The Siege of Zara, 1202 — the crusade that attacked a Christian city to pay a bill
sources: Wikipedia: Siege of Zara — the crusaders' deal with Venice was for transport of about 35,000 crusaders for 94,000 marks of silver; Venice suspended its regular commerce for a year to build and crew the ships, but only about 12,000 crusaders showed up; they could only pay 51,000 marks, even after the nobles pledged their gold and silver plate; Venice accepted the capture of Zara (Zadar), a Catholic city on the Adriatic that had rebelled against Venice and placed itself under the protection of the Pope and King Emeric of Hungary — who had himself pledged to join the crusade; the attack began in November 1202 despite letters from Pope Innocent III forbidding it and threatening excommunication; some crusaders refused and camped apart; the citizens hung flags with crosses on the walls to show they were a Christian city; the fleet burst through the harbour chains; on 13 November siege engines bombarded the walls; Zara fell on 24 November and was sacked; in 1203 Innocent III excommunicated the entire army and the Venetians (later lifting it for the non-Venetians); the campaign led on to the siege of Constantinople
Wikipedia: Enrico Dandolo — the Doge of Venice, already aged and blind, but deeply ambitious
Also on this day (candidates.md, in the app): 1871 Henry Morton Stanley finds David Livingstone; 1975 the SS Edmund Fitzgerald sinks in Lake Superior

Paintings (public domain): Andrea Vicentino, The Siege of Zara; Jacopo Tintoretto, The Conquest of Zara (1584); Zara in Konrad Grünenberg's pilgrimage book (c. 1487); Gustave Doré, Dandolo preaching the crusade; portrait engraving of Enrico Dandolo; Palma il Giovane and Delacroix, the taking of Constantinople; a 15th-century miniature of the crusader fleet; a map of Dalmatia

post.facebook:
On this day in 1202, the Fourth Crusade began the siege of Zara — a Christian city.

The crusaders had ordered a fleet from Venice big enough for 35,000 men, at 94,000 marks of silver. Venice stopped its trade for a year to build it. Only about 12,000 crusaders showed up, and they couldn't pay. Venice's aged, blind doge, Enrico Dandolo, offered a deal: help us capture Zara, the Catholic city on the Adriatic that had rebelled against us.

Zara was under the protection of the Pope and the King of Hungary — who had himself sworn to go on crusade. Pope Innocent III wrote forbidding the attack and threatening excommunication. Some crusaders refused, but most went anyway. The people of Zara hung crosses on their walls to show they were Christians too. It made no difference: the city fell on 24 November and was sacked.

The Pope excommunicated the entire army. And the crusade never reached Jerusalem — its next target was Constantinople.

youtube.description:
10 November 1202: the Fourth Crusade besieged Zara (Zadar), a Catholic city on the Adriatic. The crusaders had ordered a Venetian fleet for 35,000 men but only about 12,000 came, and they couldn't pay. The blind Doge of Venice, Enrico Dandolo, offered a deal — capture Zara for Venice. The Pope forbade it, the citizens hung crosses on their walls, and the city fell anyway. Innocent III excommunicated the whole army, and the crusade never reached Jerusalem; its next target was Constantinople.
